extracted.intended_audience: journalism students, instructors, and aspiring/early-career reporters
extracted.subtask_description: An introductory textbook-style rubric covering core newswriting and reporting skills for students and novice reporters, including print and online reporting, ethics, legal considerations, and genre-specific writing (hard news, features, editorials, obituaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: News judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows how to develop news judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a core skill the book teaches — understanding what makes something newsworthy and how to prioritize coverage; supported by examples from a range of newspapers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasized alongside fairness as a fundamental requirement for newswriting; the edition updates material to address contemporary accuracy demands in journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paired with accuracy as a principal standard for reporting; the text addresses fairness in coverage and balancing perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: How to organize a story and write it clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides on structuring stories and producing clear prose for readers; includes illustrated examples from real newspapers to model good organization and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle the complexities of honesty and ethics in journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses ethical scandals that have strained credibility and provides guidance on ethical decision-making and honesty in reporting; treated as a substantive, contemporary concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat coverage and specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cover traditional beats and prepare to specialize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaches practical strategies for beat reporting and preparing to develop subject-matter expertise as a reporter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre mastery (hard news, features, editorials, opinions)
rubrics_metrics.description: From spot or hard news to features, news features, editorials and opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the conventions and techniques for multiple news genres so writers can produce appropriate copy across formats and assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obituary writing
rubrics_metrics.description: A new section on obituary writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit dedicated coverage of obituary composition and conventions added in the second edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal awareness for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Greater emphasis on recent legal trends involving journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes material to help reporters understand legal issues that affect reporting (e.g., libel, privacy, access) and how legal trends impact journalistic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online reporting and web opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased attention to opportunities on the World Wide Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses adapting reporting and writing for the web, digital opportunities for journalists, and contemporary demands placed on reporters by online media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of real-world examples and adaptation to publication context
rubrics_metrics.description: Loaded with examples from the largest dailies to respected state capital city newspapers and campus publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages learning from diverse models and adapting writing/reporting to the scale, audience, and editorial standards of different types of publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace-ready reporting and writing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaches students the writing and reporting skills necessary in today’s job market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames instruction toward employability — practical skills and preparation intended to make students competitive for newsroom jobs and to excite them about career possibilities.
